name: Remotion Seeded Scramble And RGB Glitch Text
use_when: A short title, tech phrase, cyber moment, AMV beat, or shock reveal needs controlled glitch energy.
The agent needs deterministic jitter or scramble that renders the same way every time.
A CapCut glitch/decode look needs a Remotion equivalent.
avoid_when: The line is long, accessibility-critical, or serious documentary testimony.
The background is busy enough that RGB offsets will reduce readability.
The effect is being used repeatedly without a narrative or beat reason.

timeline_pattern.pattern: short_word -> character_or_layer_split -> seeded_random_by_frame_or_index -> scramble_or_rgb_offsets -> lock_or_resolve -> stable_readable_hold
timeline_pattern.scramble_rule: Each character locks to its target after its own threshold; unlocked characters use a controlled random character set.
timeline_pattern.glitch_rule: RGB layers should jitter from deterministic offsets and then resolve to one readable word.
timeline_pattern.stability_rule: Update jitter every 2-3 frames when every-frame jitter becomes too noisy.

motion.rule: Glitch energy should resolve quickly enough that the final word is readable before the cut.

keyframe_values.jitter_step: Change seeded glitch offsets every 2-3 frames for a readable choppy digital feel.
keyframe_values.offset_range: Keep RGB layer offsets small enough that the word silhouette remains recognizable.
keyframe_values.lock_window: Short words can lock over roughly 30 frames; shorten or simplify for fast social captions.

sound.rule: A glitch tick or short digital burst can land on the resolve frame, but it must stay below dialogue and end with the visual.

captions.rule: Do not use scramble/glitch as the only accessibility caption for important speech.

color.rule: Use controlled high-contrast RGB or accent colors; avoid accidental muddy edges from blend modes over bright footage.

implementation.ffmpeg: Approximate simple timed color changes or pre-render the Remotion glitch text as an overlay; raw drawtext is not ideal for deterministic per-character jitter.
implementation.remotion: Use seeded random values rather than Math.random; split text into characters or colored duplicate layers, drive offsets from frame/index seeds, and resolve to a stable final text layer.
implementation.blender: Use duplicate colored text objects or compositor offsets with a seeded animation driver, then resolve to a single readable layer.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use glitch/decode text presets or separate word layers with a short glitch effect, then trim the effect so final text is stable.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use duplicated RGB text layers or a tested glitch preset for short title moments; render a preview to check readability.

common_mistakes: Using non-deterministic random values that flicker differently on render.
Scrambling every frame until the word becomes unreadable.
Letting RGB offsets stay active after the reveal should be resolved.
Using random glyphs that accidentally form offensive or misleading words.
Applying glitch to serious or dense caption text.
qc: The same frame renders with the same random offsets on repeated exports.
The final word locks before the cut away.
RGB offsets preserve the word silhouette at phone size.
The glitch SFX, if used, ends with the visual resolve and stays below speech.
The effect is limited to moments where glitch matches tone and meaning.
